learning_outcomes.title: AA triangle similarity
learning_outcomes.statement: Identify similar triangles using the AA Similarity Postulate.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: Two pairs of congruent corresponding angles establish triangle similarity. Parallel lines and vertical angles can supply those angle pairs.

questions.instruction: Determine whether the triangles are similar. Choose a valid explanation.
questions.stem: Determine whether the triangles are similar. Choose a valid explanation.

options.text: Not similar: equal vertical angles prevent similarity.
Not enough information: no angle pair is known.
Similar by SSS: three side lengths are given.
Similar by AA: the marked angles and vertical angles are equal.

answer.correct_option_text: Similar by AA: the marked angles and vertical angles are equal.
answer.explanation: There is a marked equal angle pair, and the angles at H are vertical.

options.text: Not enough information: the third angles cannot be found.

answer.correct_option_text: Similar by AA: their angle sets are 42°, 98°, 40°.

questions.instruction: Determine whether the triangles are similar. Choose a valid explanation.

options.text: Definitely not similar: vertical angles have different measures.
Not enough information: only the vertical angle pair is known.
Similar by AA: a second pair is marked congruent.
Similar by SSS: all side ratios are given.

answer.correct_option_text: Not enough information: only the vertical angle pair is known.
answer.explanation: The drawing alone does not establish a second angle pair or side ratios.

questions.instruction: Determine whether the triangles are similar. Choose a valid explanation.
questions.stem: Determine whether the triangles are similar. Choose a valid explanation.

options.text: Similar by AA: both triangles have angles 87°, 41°, 52°.
Not similar: the displayed angle values differ.
Not enough information: a third angle cannot be calculated.
Similar by a scale factor of 2 shown on the sides.

answer.correct_option_text: Similar by AA: both triangles have angles 87°, 41°, 52°.
answer.explanation: Subtract 87+41 or 52+41 from 180 to get the missing angle.
